name: Cabinet
description: A lightweight self-hosted file cabinet and document manager.
summary: Cabinet v0.5.0 (2026-07-04) is the largest release since v0.4.0, delivering 238 commits with major features including Connect Knowledge (Google Drive, iCloud, OneDrive, Dropbox), a 52-connector Integrations Hub (Slack, Google, Microsoft 365, Snowflake, LinkedIn, Discord, Telegram), per-room agent Channels, a Telegram remote-control gateway, and a 'Manila Arc' borderless UI redesign. Security improvements include PBKDF2 password hashing with per-install salt and login rate-limiting. v0.6.0 introduces a self-update mechanism, with future releases published at https://github.com/cabinetai/cabinet-releases. Breaking changes include a migration from hash-based to clean-path routing and an on-disk rename of the internal team-chat directory from `.slack` to `.channels`.

answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes, v0.5.0 released 2026-07-04 with 238 commits and v0.6.0 followed shortly after
answers.Does it support user authentication?: Yes, with PBKDF2 password hashing, per-install salt, login rate-limiting, and mobile/reverse-proxy sign-in support

breaking_excerpts: Clean-path routing: the app serves clean URLs instead of hash routes across web and Electron; old hash links resolve via a marker-scan parser but the canonical form is now path-based.
Channels on-disk rename: the internal team-chat directory moved from `.slack` to `.channels`, scoped per room.
v0.6.0 moves the update mechanism to a new updater; future releases are published at https://github.com/cabinetai/cabinet-releases instead of the original repository.

alternatives.name: Paperless-ngx
alternatives.review: Paperless-ngx offers far more advanced document management with OCR and tagging but is significantly heavier and more complex to self-host than Cabinet.

alternatives.name: Docspell
alternatives.review: Docspell provides robust document organization with OCR and metadata extraction but requires more infrastructure setup compared to Cabinet's simplicity.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud
alternatives.review: Nextcloud is a full-featured cloud platform covering file management and much more, but its scope and resource requirements dwarf Cabinet's focused lightweight approach.

alternatives.name: Teedy
alternatives.review: Teedy is a feature-rich document management system with workflows and ACL support, making it more enterprise-oriented but less lightweight than Cabinet.

alternatives.name: FileRun
alternatives.review: FileRun offers a polished self-hosted file manager with user management and sharing, but its advanced features are locked behind a commercial license unlike Cabinet.
